question: Aqua regia is an acidic, corrosive and oxidative mixture consisting of ________ volume/volumes of concentrated hydrochloric acid and one volume of concentrated nitric acid, often used to dissolve gold and platinum.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aqua Regia (Latin for “royal water”) is an acidic, corrosive, and oxidative mixture of **three parts** concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl) and one part concentrated nitric acid (HNO3).
 
• Aqua regia or nitro-hydrochloric acid is a highly corrosive mixture of acids, a fuming yellow or red solution. 
 
• Aqua regia or nitro-hydrochloric acid is a highly corrosive mixture of acids, a fuming yellow or red solution.
 
• The mixture is formed by freshly mixing concentrated nitric acid and hydrochloric acid, optimally in a volume ratio of **1:3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Aqua Regia (HNO₃ + 3HCl) is **used to etch gold or platinum.**
 
• Optimally it is in a molar ratio of 1 part nitric acid to 3 parts hydrochloric acid. 
 
• When freshly mixed is clear, turns yellow very quickly and eventually red.
